kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY VOLCANO ACTIVITY NOTIFICATION
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH - A shallow intrusion occurred beneath Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit Kīlauea volcano Sep 30–Oct 1. At present there is minor spattering at both north and south vents. It is not possible to forecast the onset of episode 55 fountains or if they will occur.
kilauea_notices.detail: HVO is issuing a weekly Volcano Observatory Notice for Aviation (VONA) and associated Volcano Activity Notices (VAN) which are now required to be reissued weekly for volcanoes at ORANGE. (VONA repeat interval is daily for volcanoes at RED and every two weeks for volcanoes at YELLOW). A shallow intrusion occurred beneath Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit Kīlauea volcano September 30–October 1. Overflow activity from north and south vents stopped shortly after intrusion ended. Minor spattering resumed at north and south vents on October 5 and is continuing. These may either lead to episode 55 high fountains or, alternatively, to opening of a new vent. Forecast windows for episode 55 fountaining can no longer be modeled due to changes in conditions. Episode 54 fountaining ended at 7:33 p.m. HST on Tuesday, August 25, 2026. HVO continues to closely monitor ongoing activity. Please see the Daily Update for Kīlauea for more details. All eruptive vents and lava flows are confined to Halemaʻumaʻu crater within Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park. Tephra fall from volcanic ash clouds is greatest within 3 miles (5 km) of the vents, lighter ash and Peleʻs Hair may stay suspended for large distances from the vents. Timeline of eruptive episodes since December 23, 2024: https://www.usgs.gov/volcanoes/kilauea/science/eruption-information Three Kīlauea summit livestream videos are available here: https://www.youtube.com/@usgs/streams Additional short updates shared during the episode can be found here: https://www.usgs.gov/observatories/hvo/observatory-messages

mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
